# Ultra-Realistic Vinyl Player

> A browser turntable simulator. You load your own audio files and play them on
> a modelled record deck. It is a single static web page with no server, no
> account and no tracking; audio never leaves the device.

URL: https://gitguy268-ultra-realistic-vinyl-player.vercel.app/
Source: https://github.com/Gitguy268/realistic-vinyl-player
License: MIT

## What it does

- Plays local audio files (anything the browser can decode) through a Web Audio
  chain that models a turntable: a motor that spins up and coasts down, pitch
  control of plus or minus 8 percent, RIAA playback equalisation, and wow and
  flutter.
- Draws the deck on a canvas: platter, strobe ring, record and tonearm. The
  tonearm can be dragged onto the record, or moved with the keyboard.
- Lets you scratch: dragging the record plays the audio by hand, forward or
  backward. This works for files up to 150 MiB; larger files stream instead.
- Adds optional synthesized surface noise with a wear control.
- Keeps a library and a queue in the browser's IndexedDB, with tags, cover art,
  shuffle, repeat and optional auto-advance.
- Can show a visualizer on the record label while a record plays: MilkDrop
  (butterchurn), spectrum bars after Musializer, a ridgeline, an
  oscilloscope, a spectrogram or a radial spectrum. It is off by default.
- Has a Winamp-style ten-band graphic EQ with Winamp's presets, and loads
  Winamp .eqf preset files.
- Can show the library as a desktop, with artists and albums as folders.
- Works offline after the first visit and can be installed as an app.

## What it does not do

- It does not stream music from any service and ships with no audio.
- It does not upload, analyse or share files.
- It is not a measurement-grade emulation: the equalisation departs from the
  ideal RIAA curve above about 10 kHz, and nothing here was tuned against real
  hardware.

## Controls

Space plays or lifts the needle. L moves the cue lever, M the motor. Left and
right arrows seek five seconds; up and down change the volume. S toggles
shuffle, R cycles repeat, F toggles focus mode, and ? lists every shortcut.
